Q: Does returning 0 signal successful execution for all functions? A:

Returning zero is a convention, especially in Unix world. If a program (so it's main() function) returns zero, it means it finished successfully. Other values can (not neccesarily though) mean an error. You can see sysexits.h for a list of common return codes.

Also, if you miss return statement, main() will still (implicitly) return zero (valid for C++). It is defined in C++ standard, 3.6.1 point 5:

If control reaches the end of main without encountering a return statement, the eﬀect is that of executing return 0;

In shell, ex. Bash, you can check what value has been returned from main() by looking at $? variable, on example:

$ g++ prog.cpp
$ ./a.out
$ echo $?
0

For functions other than main() you should remember that zero, in comparison, is a boolean false, so returning zero may not be intepreted as a success (or true). But the return value can be anything and, in general, it does not have any special meaning, so returning zero is okay.

Q: Why can a function be invoked without assigning its return value anywhere? A:

In C/C++, a function may choose its return type as void or some specific type. However, if non-void is the return type of a function, whenever the function is called, the caller may or may not use the return value. That does not necessary mean this is equivalent to void return type. You have the option of checking the return value, but you don't need to check that, upto you, optional. Hope that answers.

Q: Why does dovecot on localhost repeat "Disconnected (no auth attempts in 0 secs)"? A:

I have a similar issue. I am using dovecot 2.3 on freebsd with auth from postfix (/var/spool/postfix/private/auth) and 993 ssl only (no 143/tcp). imap works fine while reading email on folders. However when copying sent mail to Sent Maildir folder, it fails with either timeout or network error. I did enable imap_client_workarounds for thunderbird but that doesn't change anything, my problem doesn't seem to be related to that whatsoever.

Normal imaps operations work fine when reading email.

I also see those messages once in a while

imap-login: Disconnected: Connection closed (no auth attempts in 101 secs): user=<>, ...

which confirms some kind of timeout but on the server side.

I tried with Sylpheed and there's no issue at all. After sending the message, it gets copied alright to Sent folder.

So there's two options here:

  1. It's a bug specific to Dovecot<>Thunderbird

  2. it's a DPI-capable firewall in between which falsly considers that copying-sent-mail as an ssl-vpn tunnel and blocks it. it's an option as I am in a country with restricted internet

All I have to offer are workarounds:

  • setup sent mail to be copied to a local folder in Account settings

  • --or-- enable SOCKSv5 or whatnot proxy in General / Network settings (this goes for the whole profile covering all accounts)

Q: Workers in Playwright with parallel execution true is not working properly A:

With Playwright, enabling parallel execution means multiple workers may run tests at the same time, so any shared state can become a source of intermittent failures.

I’d first check whether the tests share browser context, pages, test data, files, ports, or accounts. Each worker should generally get its own isolated browserContext/page and independent test data. Also make sure you are not storing mutable state in module-level variables or reusing a single page across tests.

If the problem only appears when workers > 1, try running the same tests with workers: 1. If they pass consistently, that strongly suggests a race condition or shared resource rather than Playwright itself. The exact error and the relevant playwright.config plus test code would be needed to determine which resource is conflicting.

Q: What is the difference between year and year-of-era? A:

The answer lies in the documentation for IsoChronology.

  • era - There are two eras, "Current Era" (CE) and "Before Current Era" (BCE).
  • year-of-era - The year-of-era is the same as the proleptic-year for the current CE era. For the BCE era before the ISO epoch the year increases from 1 upwards as time goes backwards.
  • proleptic-year - The proleptic year is the same as the year-of-era for the current era. For the previous era, years have zero, then negative values.

u will give you the proleptic year. y will give you the year of the era.

The difference is mainly important for years of the BC era. The proleptic year 0 is actually 1 BC, it is followed by proleptic year 1 which is 1 AD. The proleptic year can be negative, the year of era can not.

proleptic era
3 3 AD
2 2 AD
1 1 AD
0 1 BC
-1 2 BC
-2 3 BC
-3 4 BC

Here is a Java snippet to generate this data:

DateTimeFormatter formatter = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("'proleptic' : u '= era:' y G");

for (int i = 3; i > -4 ; i--) {
    LocalDate localDate = LocalDate.of(i, 3, 14);
    System.out.println(formatter.format(localDate));
}

Output:

proleptic : 3 = era: 3 AD
proleptic : 2 = era: 2 AD
proleptic : 1 = era: 1 AD
proleptic : 0 = era: 1 BC
proleptic : -1 = era: 2 BC
proleptic : -2 = era: 3 BC
proleptic : -3 = era: 4 BC

Q: How can I add an iFrame to Powerapps? A:

Welcome to the world of PowerApps development :)

Fun question but you should provide more details in the future:

  1. What kind of PowerApp? Canvas or Model App?
  2. What component did you try? Share the link and how / where you used it.
  3. What will be hosted in the iFrame? Are you going to run into CORS issues? What is the aim of adding this iFrame?

Here are some pointers, but without more details I don't know if its the right solution.

If its a model app you can do it via the form editor: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/iframe-properties-legacy

If its a canvas app you'll need to add a custom component: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/component-framework/sample-controls/iframe-control

Good luck!

Q: Elasticsearch with xpack security fails A:

I got this issue when the data folder of ElasticSearch was deleted and re-initialized from scratch afterwards. The point is that the built-in users were not initialized.

As soon as I initialized the built-in users the error disappeared and the system worked again.

bin/elasticsearch-setup-passwords interactive|auto [-u "https://<host_name>:9200"]
